item.title: Destruction of a Lake – a Ramsar Site – in India’s Northeast
item.description: Construction activity, effluents and sewage are destroying the Deepor Beel in Assam.

item.title: Modi Government Strikes Hard on Indian Workers
item.description: Earlier, government permission was required to sack 100 employees or more. Now, no permission is required for sacking up to 300 employees.

item.title: Is Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League Returning to Politics Under New Leadership?
item.description: Party offices in some districts have been reopened, and national and party flags are being raised.

item.title: Why Was a Kazakh Lawyer Stripped of His License?
item.description: Murat Adam tried to defend the rights of his client, an editor under fire, and found himself in the state’s crosshairs.

item.title: Revelations of Chinese Nuclear Tests Mark Start of a New Era
item.description: While China is expanding its nuclear arsenal at a dramatic pace, Russia and the U.S. are also testing new delivery platforms.

item.title: China, ASEAN, and Beyond: The UK Strategy for the Indo-Pacific
item.description: “Euro-Atlantic security and prosperity depends on a free and open Indo-Pacific,” writes U.K. Minister for the Indo-Pacific Seema Malhotra.

item.title: New US Tariffs, Same Problems for Japan, South Korea, and Taiwan
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court’s tariff ruling only adds uncertainty for the U.S. partners in East Asia.

item.title: Where Did Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Disappear To? And Why Does It Matter?
item.description: Rahmon surfaced after an apparent 17-day absence on February 14. His stepping out of the limelight stirred up rumors of ill health.

item.title: Why Japan Must Help Counter China’s Presence in the Pacific
item.description: From elite capture to organized crime, China’s influence is growing in Micronesia. Japan is uniquely positioned to help combat this trend.

item.title: Nepal’s Gen Z Election
item.description: Biswas Baral discusses the Gen Z Revolution, the new crop of favorites – headed by Kathmandu Mayor Balendra Shah – and the fate of the old political forces.
